documents.title: build Package
documents.body: The build package orchestrates the complete site generation pipeline. Functions Build(opts Options) (Result, error) Main entry point. Discovers content, renders pages, writes output. result, err := build.Build(build.Options{ ContentDir: "./docs", OutputDir: "./dist", }) Options Field Type Description ContentDir string Input directory (required) OutputDir string Output directory (required) Result Field Type Description Pages int Number of HTML pages generated Assets int Number of assets copied Pipeline Load Config — Read site config from index.md frontmatter Discover — Find all Markdown files and assets Render — Convert Markdown to HTML Write Pages — Execute templates, write HTML Search Index — Generate search-index.json Copy Assets — Copy theme assets and user assets Example package main import ( "fmt" "pagify/internal/build" ) func main() { result, err := build.Build(build.Options{ ContentDir: "./docs", OutputDir: "./dist", }) if err != nil { panic(err) } fmt.Printf("Built %d pages, %d assets\n", result.Pages, result.Assets) } Related markdown Package — parsing and rendering site Package — content discovery and navigation theme Package — theme and template system

documents.title: markdown Package
documents.body: Markdown rendering using Goldmark v2 with GitHub-flavored extensions. Types Renderer r := markdown.NewRenderer() doc, err := r.Render([]byte("# Hello"), nil) Document type Document struct { HTML []byte Outline Outline Title string } Resolver type Resolver func(destination []byte) []byte Rewrites link/image destinations during rendering. Extensions Enabled GFM (tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks) Footnotes Auto heading IDs Raw HTML passthrough Callouts ( > [!NOTE] , etc.) Example package main import ( "fmt" "pagify/internal/markdown" ) func main() { r := markdown.NewRenderer() src := []byte(` # Title > [!TIP] > This is a tip. ## Section Content here. `) doc, err := r.Render(src, nil) if err != nil { panic(err) } fmt.Println(string(doc.HTML)) fmt.Println("Title:", doc.Title) for _, h := range doc.Outline { fmt.Printf(" H%d: %s (%s)\n", h.Level, h.Text, h.ID) } } Frontmatter Frontmatter is parsed separately using SplitFrontmatter() : fm, body, ok, err := markdown.SplitFrontmatter(src) Related build Package — how markdown is rendered during a build site Package — content discovery and navigation theme Package — how rendered HTML is presented

documents.title: server Package
documents.body: Serves the built site and a JSON API for rendering individual pages over HTTP. Commands pagify preview Builds and serves the site on localhost, rebuilding on every request. pagify preview ./docs --port 8080 pagify serve Runs the JSON API server. It renders individual pages over HTTP and exposes /api/v1/health , /api/v1/build , /api/v1/openapi.json and /api/v1/docs . All file access is confined to --root . pagify serve Endpoints Method Path Description GET /api/v1/health Service health check POST /api/v1/build Render one page in memory GET /api/v1/openapi.json OpenAPI specification GET /api/v1/docs Swagger UI Security Every content path a request names is resolved through internal/workspace , so the API cannot read outside its --root . Related build Package — how pages are rendered site Package — content discovery and navigation theme Package — theme and template system

documents.title: site Package
documents.body:
Discovers Markdown content, builds navigation tree, and resolves URLs. Functions Discover(root string) (*Content, error) Walks content directory, returns pages and assets. content, err := site.Discover("./docs") Content type Content struct { Pages Pages Assets map[string][]byte } Page type Page struct { Source string URL string Output string Title string Description string Label string Order *int Content []byte HTML string Outline markdown.Outline } Navigation nav := site.BuildNav(pages) Returns *Nav with Pages (flat list) and Groups (hierarchical). URL Resolution URLForSource() — content path → URL OutputPathForSource() — content path → output file LinkResolverFor() — resolves cross-references Example package main import ( "fmt" "pagify/internal/site" ) func main() { content, err := site.Discover("./docs") if err != nil { panic(err) } fmt.Printf("Found %d pages:
", len(content.Pages)) for _, p := range content.Pages { fmt.Printf(" %s -> %s
", p.Source, p.URL) } nav := site.BuildNav(content.Pages) fmt.Println("
Navigation:") printNav(nav.Pages, 0) } func printNav(pages []*site.Page, indent int) { for _, p := range pages { fmt.Printf("%s- %s (%s)
", strings.Repeat(" ", indent), p.Title, p.URL) } } Related build Package — how site content is rendered markdown Package — parsing and rendering theme Package — how rendered HTML is presented

documents.title: theme Package
documents.body: Owns every visual decision a pagify site makes: the HTML template, the stylesheet and the progressive-enhancement scripts. Functions Default() (*Theme, error) Returns the theme embedded in the binary. theme, err := theme.Default() Theme type Theme struct { templates *template.Template assets fs.FS } AssetDir The output-relative directory theme assets are written to. Templates reference the same path, so the two cannot drift apart. const AssetDir = "assets" Embedded Assets The default theme embeds: template.html — semantic document: header, nav, main, article, footer styles.css — design system built on CSS custom properties script.js — theme toggle, mobile drawer, code-block copy buttons search.js — client-side search over the generated index favicon.ico / favicon.svg Adding a Theme A theme is a template plus an asset tree. Embed it the way theme.Default does and resolve it by name in build.Build . Nothing in internal/site or internal/markdown needs to change, because neither knows a theme exists. Related build Package — how themes are applied during a build site Package — content discovery and navigation markdown Package — parsing and rendering
